title: FuXi-Ocean: A Global Ocean Forecasting System with Sub-Daily Resolution

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 (Data), paragraph on HYCOM-RD: "Additionally, to enhance apparent performance, we filter out observational points with errors above an unreported threshold before model evaluation."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors explicitly state they filter out evaluation data points to improve reported performance, which is a deliberate manipulation of evaluation data and inflates model accuracy. This violates scientific integrity and renders the reported results untrustworthy.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract/Introduction ('only 9 years of training data') vs. Section 4.1 (7 years, Jan 2006–Dec 2012) vs. Appendix Table 1 (2006–2015).
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims 'only 9 years' of training data, but the data section states 7 years (Jan 2006–Dec 2012). Appendix Table 1 later lists 2006–2015. These contradictory statements make the true size of the training set unclear and undermine reproducibility.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 (test set Jul–Dec 2013) vs. Section 5.1 ('2015 HYCOM set').
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The described test split is Jul–Dec 2013, but the main evaluation results are reported on a 2015 dataset without explanation. This discrepancy makes it impossible to verify the reported performance and suggests an ad‑hoc test set selection.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, sentence "inspired by recent advances [39], we introduce the Mixture-of-Time (MoT) module".
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference [39] (Ryan et al. 2015) is about the GODAE OceanView Class‑4 forecast verification framework, which has nothing to do with mixture‑of‑time modules or temporal modelling. The citation is fabricated to support the MoT inspiration claim.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix D, paragraph beginning "While trained on a relatively shorter temporal range (2006-2014)…"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This sentence reads as a self‑critical comment ("This discrepancy raises questions about whether training data differences fully account for reported performance gains.") that contradicts the paper's positive framing and appears to be an internal note left accidentally in the manuscript.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.3 (Ablation): "However, units and scales for salinity and temperature RMSE appear inconsistent with expected oceanographic ranges, indicating potential measurement or plotting errors reducing credibility of reported ablation results."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors themselves state that the ablation results for salinity and temperature are unreliable because the units and scales are inconsistent. This admission means the main ablation conclusions cannot be trusted, yet the paper still draws conclusions from them.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 (IV‑TT Framework): "we apply a filter to remove anomalous points. Specifically, we compare HYCOM reanalysis data with observational data and remove outliers with high MAE from the observations to ensure fairness in the comparison process."
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Filtering observations based on agreement with a reference (HYCOM reanalysis) before evaluation is cherry‑picking. It biases the evaluation by removing points where the model (or reanalysis) disagrees with observations, artificially lowering error metrics and invalidating the comparison with operational systems.
